name: Download each resume directly, named after the applicant, and report the file it actually wrote
request: Download each resume directly, named after the applicant, and report the file it actually wrote
checks: npm run check passed (typecheck, build, 393 tests, validate)
result: The saved resume is now named after the applicant instead of after LinkedIn's media id, and it is downloaded rather than previewed. The naming policy is pure and lives in applicants-core.js so the cases that actually break a save are tested rather than hoped for: sanitizeFileName() replaces / \ : * ? " < > | with a space rather than deleting them (so Ann/Marie does not become AnnMarie), strips C0 controls and DEL, collapses whitespace, strips leading dots and trailing dots or spaces (a leading dot hides the file on Unix, a trailing one is silently dropped by Windows), caps the stem at 100 characters and appends ' file' to a Windows device name because CON.pdf is not a file. It returns a stem only - never a path - so ../../etc/passwd cannot come out of it. resumeFileExtension() takes pdf, .PDF, application/pdf, a filename or the URL, and returns '' rather than guessing; resumeFileName() welds stem + suffix + extension, and an unknown type yields no extension at all plus an extraction warning, because a .pdf on a .docx is a lie written to the recruiter's disk. Duplicates: the worker keeps a register of which applicant claimed which stem, so the second DIFFERENT person of a name gets ' (2)' while the same person collected twice keeps their own file rather than growing a suffix every visit; Chrome's uniquify stays as the on-disk backstop, and Clear Applicants clears the register. localReference is now read back from chrome.downloads.search rather than assumed, so resume_file shows the file Chrome actually wrote even when uniquify renamed it. And collectResume now looks for the document address BEFORE clicking anything - the control's own href, then every rendered document attribute across panel and page - and downloads straight to disk when it finds one, opening the viewer only when the page has not rendered the address and closing it immediately. That is rule 9e as written (a link needs no click) and it is what 'download, do not preview' asked for; the click budget is unchanged at five.
